 An overview of this role
 As a Security Analyst on GitLab’s Product Security Vulnerability Operations team, you will help protect GitLab customers by triaging security reports, supporting vulnerability management operations, and coordinating clear communications with security researchers, customers, and internal teams.
 You will work closely with PSIRT engineers, Vulnerability Management, Security Engineering, Legal, Customer Success, Support, and Communications. This role is an excellent opportunity for an early-career security prfessional who is curious, organized, detail-oriented, and excited to build expertise in product security response.
 This role is open to candidates across North America, though we encourage applications from those based on the West Coast US or West Coast Canada (British Columbia) as the team is looking to expand coverage in the Pacific Time Zone. 
 What you’ll do
 Triage incoming bug bounty reports, including reviewing report quality, validating findings, assessing potential impact, identifying duplicates, and routing reports to the appropriate teams.
 Triage vulnerabilities identified through vulnerability management activities and help track them through assessment, remediation, and closure.
 Work with PSIRT engineers and development teams to gather technical details, reproduce issues, and clarify affected products, versions, and configurations.
 Support severity assessment using frameworks and terminology such as CVE, CVSS, CWE, and OWASP.
 Communicate professionally and respectfully with security researchers participating in coordinated vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty programs.
 Support GitLab’s role as a CVE Numbering Authority by preparing information for CVE assignment, maintaining accurate records, and helping coordinate CVE-related activities.
 Represent GitLab as an acting CNA representative in CVE-related discussions and operations, escalating questions and coordinating with the appropriate internal and external stakeholders.
 Draft and coordinate customer-facing communications about security vulnerabilities, fixes, mitigations, and release information in partnership with PSIRT, Legal, Customer Success, Support, and Corporate Communications.
 Maintain accurate issue records, timelines, researcher communications, remediation status, and follow-up actions.
 Monitor queues and operational metrics to identify trends, aging items, recurring issues, and opportunities to improve response quality and consistency.
 Create and improve runbooks, procedures, templates, and other documentation that make vulnerability handling more efficient and transparent.
 Participate in incident handoffs, root cause analysis documentation, lessons-learned activities, and product security reviews.
 Build technical and operational expertise in PSIRT, bug bounty, vulnerability management, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure.
 What you’ll bring
 Early-career experience or equivalent education in cybersecurity, software engineering, information technology, or a related field. Relevant internships, coursework, labs, research, customer support, or practical security projects are welcome.
 Foundational understanding of software vulnerabilities and security concepts, including web applications, APIs, CI/CD environments, authentication, and authorization.
 Familiarity with security terminology such as CVE, CVSS, CWE, OWASP Top 10, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure.
 Strong attention to detail and the ability to organize and prioritize multiple reports or work items.
 Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical topics to both technical and non-technical audiences.
 Experience with a bug bounty or vulnerability disclosure platform such as HackerOne or Bugcrowd.
 Experience reviewing security reports, participating in capture-the-flag exercises, performing vulnerability research, or working with security tooling.
 Familiarity with CVE assignment, CNA processes, security advisories, or vulnerability databases.
 Nice to have: Basic scripting, log analysis, issue tracking, or data analysis experience; experience writing technical documentation, customer communications, support responses, or operational procedures.
 About the team
 The GitLab Product Security Vulnerability Operations is a globally distributed team that helps ensure GitLab delivers secure applications customers can trust. VulnOps serves as a central point of contact for external security researchers and helps govern the policies, processes, and guidelines used to address vulnerabilities in GitLab’s supported products.
 Team members collaborate across regions using documented processes, automation, and structured handoffs to support vulnerability resolution and ongoing operational improvements.

We're looking for a strategic, data-driven Head of User Acquisition to own how Phoenix acquires customers across paid and organic channels. Paid media will be the core of this role - you'll set strategy, assist in the execution, own the budget, and build the team driving performance across Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, Reddit, etc. You’ll also oversee SEO/AEO, affiliates, and partnerships as complementary acquisition levers. This is a senior, cross-channel role: you're accountable for the full acquisition mix, not just one channel in isolation.

You'll set acquisition strategy end-to-end: channel investment priorities, team structure, and the frameworks that connect paid, organic, and partnership-driven growth into one coherent acquisition engine. Paid Media

 - Own budget planning and pacing across all paid channels, making tradeoff decisions to maximize efficient growth.

 - Set audience strategy, segmentation, and experimentation roadmap for paid campaigns.

 - Build and scale retargeting and remarketing strategy across paid channels.

Organic & AEO/SEO

 - Own SEO and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) strategy, ensuring Phoenix and Raven are discoverable across both traditional search and generative/AI-driven search surfaces.

 - Set organic content and technical SEO priorities in partnership with content, brand, and product teams.

Cross-Channel Leadership

 - Build and lead the user acquisition team, hiring, mentoring, and developing specialists across paid, organic, and partnerships as the function scales.

 - Set the analytics and reporting framework across all acquisition channels, translating data into strategic recommendations for executive leadership.

 - Partner with creative, product, and brand leadership to align acquisition strategy with broader company positioning and growth goals.

 - Working knowledge of SEO fundamentals and familiarity with AEO/GEO (Answer Engine Optimization / Generative Engine Optimization) as an emerging discipline.

 - Experience developing or managing partnership-driven acquisition channels is a plus.

 - Proven track record scaling paid acquisition with measurable impact on CAC, ROAS, and revenue growth.

 - Strong strategic and analytical mindset — comfortable moving between high-level strategy and campaign-level detail.

 - Experience managing budgets and making cross-channel investment tradeoffs at scale.

 - Track record of cross-functional leadership, influencing creative, product, and executive stakeholders.

 Position Overview 
 This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role. You will spend most of your week writing test code, building test infrastructure, and working directly with engineers, not writing test plans for others to execute.
 We are looking for someone to take our test automation and quality engineering practices to the next level. You will build the automated test suites and tooling underneath them, raise the standard for how the engineering team tests its own work, and help ensure our quality practices keep pace with how quickly modern software is now developed.
 Software gets written and changed faster than it did even a few years ago. AI-assisted development accelerates that further, but it also changes where defects come from and what traditional reviews and test suites may miss. We want someone who sees that as an engineering problem: building the coverage, tooling, feedback loops, and development practices that allow the team to move quickly without sacrificing reliability.
 Our products also increasingly include AI and machine-learning functionality, including LLM-based assistants and integrations with AI clients. These systems introduce a different class of testing problem. Outputs may vary between runs, model or prompt changes can alter behaviour without traditional code changes, and quality may need to be measured across a set of results rather than with a simple pass or fail.
 You do not need to be an ML researcher, but you should have experience testing software with AI, ML, LLM, or other non-deterministic components and understand how to build credible evidence that these systems are ready to ship.

 Keep automated testing fast, reliable, and useful enough that developers trust it and use it regularly
 Build API and contract testing across services and integration boundaries

 Investigate and debug difficult failures across application, service, database, infrastructure, and deployment boundaries
 Work with engineers to determine appropriate test coverage and validation approaches for new features and systems
 Review test code with the same engineering standards applied to production code
 Help developers improve the quality and testability of their own code rather than making testing the responsibility of a separate QA silo

 Identify gaps in existing test coverage and determine where deeper or different forms of validation are required
 Help adapt our testing practices to the increased pace and changing failure modes introduced by AI-assisted software development
 Use modern development and AI tooling to improve the speed and effectiveness of test development while maintaining confidence in the results
 Validate that automated tests actually detect incorrect behaviour rather than simply confirming the current implementation
 Share testing practices, tooling, and lessons across the engineering team
 AI and ML Quality

 Test non-deterministic systems using representative datasets, repeated evaluation, appropriate metrics, and acceptance thresholds

 Quarterly Town Halls and Kickoffs that bring teams together to celebrate wins, share updates, and look ahead at what’s next
 Apply Now! 
 If you’re looking for a place where your work touches real products, real customers, and real decisions, and where your career can grow in the direction you choose. We would love to meet you. Apply and let’s talk about what’s possible.  
 Accessibility & AI Transparency

Senior TAMs are part of the Engineering team and collaborate closely with Affirm's Product, Engineering, Operations, Customer Success, and Frontline Technical Support teams.
 This is an operations-heavy role to start. Expect the majority of your early focus to be on keeping merchant integrations healthy—monitoring, triage, troubleshooting, and SLA delivery—while you progressively take on more custom solutioning and cross-functional initiatives. Over your first 6–12 months, as you build operational mastery, you will grow into owning your own book of accounts and carrying it through to end-to-end account ownership.
 A Senior TAM independently owns operational health across the strategic alliance portfolio, designs custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations, drives cross-team collaboration on initiatives, acts as a technical lead on team projects, and mentors less-experienced members of the team.
 What You'll Do
 Own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio—alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and fielding technical inquiries—so integrations stay healthy and issues are resolved quickly.
 Deliver against SLAs, proactively surfacing technical risks before they become customer-impacting and responding with urgency to merchant issues.
 Perform in-depth investigations and root-cause analysis across logs, queries, and integration data, owning resolution end to end and escalating to cross-functional partners or executives when needed.
 Drive technical initiatives and partner with internal and merchant stakeholders on launch initiatives—expansions, promotions, new product adoption, and integration optimizations—that grow the value of the accounts after launch.
 Design and deliver high-scope, often-custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations—combining, extending, and tailoring them to complex, open-ended problems while balancing speed, quality, maintainability, reliability, and scalability.
 Act as a technical lead for internal projects, defining and delivering well-scoped milestones and executing the project roadmap.
 Operationalize best practices by creating and updating playbooks, runbooks, alerting, and UAT certification plans across the strategic alliance portfolio and continuously reduce keep-the-lights-on (KTLO) work.
 Partner with Product and Engineering leads to identify, plan, and prioritize projects based on team goals and resources, acting as the voice of the merchant to influence the roadmap.
 Mentor and level up less-experienced TAMs, share learnings from your integrations and investigations, and contribute to interviewing and team development.
 Over your first 6–12 months, grow into owning a dedicated book of strategic alliance accounts—carrying operational ownership through to end-to-end account ownership.

 Professional Background: at least six years in a technical, external-facing role such as Technical Account Management, Solutions/Partner Engineering, or Solutions Architecture—ideally within FinTech, payments, or SaaS—with a demonstrated track record of owning the operational health of technical accounts and delivering against SLAs.

ABOUT THIS ROLE

As Ashby’s first Demo Engineer, you’ll own the systems that make our demo environments reliable, current, and tailored — the infrastructure the entire go-to-market team leans on to show Ashby at its best. Today, AEs and SEs maintain and configure their own demo accounts by hand. That doesn’t scale: reps lose selling time, demos drift out of date, and every new product release widens the gap between what Ashby can do and what we can actually show live. Your job is to close that gap.

This is a net-new role. Right now, the work is split between ad hoc effort and a new set of disposable demo templates the Internal Platform team is building. You’ll own the layer on top of that foundation — customizing and extending those templates, generating realistic demo data, tailoring environments for specific verticals and new markets, and making sure every feature is demoable before it ships. You’ll sit within Solutions Engineering, reporting to the Global Head of Solutions Engineering, and partner closely with Internal Platform and Product teams.

Your work will be split roughly 70/30: about 70% owning, customizing, and extending the demo template system and the data and content inside it, and about 30% running demo readiness as a program — release readiness, documentation, and enablement so the GTM team always has current, credible demos to work with.

The best person for this job is genuinely hands-on technical — working with internal tools and configuration files, using APIs, and general data preparation — who gets energy from building leverage for a whole team rather than fixing one demo at a time.




YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF:

 - 🛠 You’re comfortable working in JSON, calling REST / developer APIs, using AI tools, and scripting to configure and customize environments.

 - 🏗 You’re a builder, not just an operator. You get energy from creating systems and tooling that make a whole team more effective over time.

 - 🎥 You care deeply about demo quality. You understand what makes a product demo land, and you’re thoughtful about data realism and the narrative a demo needs to support.

 - 🧠 You have strong product intuition and can learn a deeply configurable product quickly, understanding how the different pieces connect.

 - 🔁 You have an iterative mindset. You like testing what works, refining over time, and improving based on what you learn from the field.

 - 🧩 You’re a systems thinker who would rather standardize and automate than manually repeat the same setup.

 - ⚡ You’re comfortable with ambiguity and enjoy a 0→1 role where the infrastructure is still being built around you.

 - 🤝 You partner well cross-functionally — with Engineering and with GTM — and can translate their needs into reliable systems.

 - 💙 You have empathy for the go-to-market teams you support and the Talent Acquisition space they sell into.




BONUS POINTS FOR:

 - 📊 You’ve built demo environments, demo data, or sandbox/trial environments at a SaaS company before.

 - 🧰 You’ve written automation scripts or tooling to generate data or configure environments at scale.

 - 🎬 You’ve built and maintained a library of reusable, templated environments or assets that others relied on.

 - 🤝 You have experience with HR tech, ATS workflows, or recruiting operations.




EXAMPLES OF THINGS YOU’LL WORK ON:

 - 🧱 Own the scaled demo system — customize and extend the demo environment infrastructure to support the GTM team.

 - 🗂 Generate realistic demo data — standardize and automate how demo environments are populated to eliminate manual setup.

 - 🎯 Build vertical- and market-specific demos — create tailored content for target verticals and additional languages as we move upmarket and expand internationally.

 - 🚦 Own demo readiness for new releases — make sure every feature is correctly configured and demoable in demo environments before it ships to GA.

 - 🧪 Stand up trial and sandbox environments — create templated environments prospects can use to test Ashby during the sales cycle.

 - 📚 Document how it all works — maintain clear documentation so the GTM team knows when and how to use each demo environment.




WHY BECOME A DEMO ENGINEER AT ASHBY?

You’ll define a role that doesn’t exist yet. This is a net-new role designed around a real business need. You won’t inherit a mature playbook — you’ll build the infrastructure that lets the whole GTM team demo at a higher level.

Your work will compound. A great live demo helps one deal. A reliable, current, well-documented demo system improves every demo the entire go-to-market team runs. If you like creating leverage, this role has a lot of it.

The product gives you something real to work with. Ashby has strong product-market fit, and that matters here. You’re not manufacturing excitement around a weak product — you’re making it effortless to show something that already resonates when it’s shown well.

You’ll sit at the intersection of Engineering and GTM. This is a rare blend of technical building and understanding what the field actually needs. You’ll help translate our product releases into live deals — and connect the two.

The surface area keeps growing. As we ship new features and expand into new product areas, new verticals, and new geographies, demo needs compound with each release. There is a lot to build, and it only gets more interesting.




REASONS YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY:

 - If you want to be customer-facing or closing deals, this isn’t the right role — the impact here happens behind the scenes.

 - If you’re not genuinely hands-on technical — comfortable in JSON, APIs, and data — the core of this job will be frustrating.

 - If you need a fully built environment and a finished playbook, the ambiguity of a 0→1 role with infrastructure still being built will feel uncomfortable.

 - If continuously maintaining and updating environments as the product changes sounds tedious rather than satisfying, this won’t be a fit.

 - If you’d rather build production product features than internal tooling and demo systems, you’ll likely want a different engineering role.




INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our interview process is thorough — we want to make sure this role is the right fit for you and that you’re the right fit for Ashby. Details on the process for this role will be shared by your recruiter.




BENEFITS

 - You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

 - Sell a product that our customers are truly excited about.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby — do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!).
